decision: A billboard for the newest series with its match percentage, Play and My list, the browse pattern popularized by streaming apps
why: Learners come back to continue, not to search; the billboard sells the one new thing without a carousel of banners.
alternative: A course catalog grid with filters first.
value: One clear next action on arrival; the preview is SVG and can be paused.

decision: Continue watching shows progress bars, and the card expands after a 300 ms hover (or on focus) to offer Resume and Practice in Arena
why: Watching is not learning; the expanded card puts the matching drill one click away.
value: Lessons turn into practice sessions (drill starts per lesson view, target [value]).

decision: The Top 5 row uses outlined giant numerals drawn with text-stroke, so the rank is part of the layout rather than an image
why: The numeral reads at a glance and costs nothing to render; stroke-only keeps it from competing with the art.
alternative: Rank badges on the corner of each card.
value: Social proof without extra assets, and the numbers stay crisp at any size.

decision: Card artwork is generated per title and re-drawn to emphasize the member's weakest rubric area (Estimation from session 14 shows the numbers)
why: Personalized artwork, popularized by streaming apps, raises clicks when it reflects what the viewer cares about; here it reflects what they need to practice.
value: The same catalog nudges each member toward their gap, and they can see and change the reason.

decision: All artwork is inline SVG from a motif and an overlay, themed by tokens
why: Four rubric areas × every title would be dozens of images; SVG variants are a few hundred bytes each and follow the theme.
alternative: A pre-rendered image per title and area.
value: Zero image requests on the page, and new titles get art for free.

decision: Top 5 ranks by completed episodes followed by a drill in the last 7 days, not by views
why: Views reward thumbnails; completion plus practice rewards lessons that actually help.
value: The row promotes lessons that move rubric scores.
